candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — long-term lifestyle self-management in chronic heart failure
candidate.educational_objective: Reinforce long-term heart-failure self-care through individualized physical activity, smoking avoidance, heart-healthy nutrition, and safe counseling about alcohol use alongside prescribed medical therapy.

options.A: Remain physically active within the individualized plan, avoid smoking, follow the recommended heart-healthy diet, and discuss alcohol use with the health care team rather than assuming it is harmless.
options.B: Lifestyle habits matter mainly before heart failure develops, so they have little role once the diagnosis is established.
options.C: Avoid routine physical activity because exercise is generally unsafe once a client has chronic heart failure.
options.D: Continue smoking or heavy alcohol use if medications control symptoms because lifestyle choices no longer affect heart-failure management.

candidate.rationale: Current American Heart Association heart-failure guidance recommends appropriate regular physical activity, tobacco avoidance, and a heart-healthy dietary pattern as ongoing self-care. AHA guidance also advises clients to discuss alcohol use with their health care professional; current cardiovascular dietary guidance states that people who do not drink alcohol should not start, and those who do drink should limit intake. These habits remain relevant after the diagnosis and complement medical therapy. Therefore, A is correct. B incorrectly limits lifestyle management to prevention, C promotes unnecessary inactivity, and D dismisses established cardiovascular risks.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Directly supports ongoing physical activity, smoking cessation/avoidance, heart-healthy eating, and individualized counseling about alcohol as part of chronic heart-failure self-management.
candidate.source_document_title: Lifestyle Changes for Heart Failure; 2026 Dietary Guidance to Improve Cardiovascular Health; 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure
